Hi all — quick triage update from infra:

Summary so far:
- Incident INC-2987 opened (ops lead: Marissa Cole).
- Observed elevated 5xxs concentrated on a subset of Artemis-3B hosts in us-west-2.
- Root cause appears to be a KV cache eviction loop triggered by a recently deployed kernel selection heuristic (deploy at 14:47 UTC). When the heuristic mis-classified longer ctx requests it caused excessive KV cache churn and synchronous fallback paths that saturated request queues, producing 502/504s.

Immediate mitigations applied at 15:58 UTC:
- Rolled back the kernel-selection tweak for Artemis-3B on affected host pool.
- Increased request queue backpressure thresholds temporarily to shed load gracefully.
- Enabled prefix-KV pinning for high-throughput accounts (including Acme) to reduce cache thrash.

Visible impact: error rate reduced from ~14% to ~2.1% within ~12 minutes after the rollback; by 16:10 UTC the bulk of traffic was healthy. We're still monitoring for residual tails.

Attachments: artemis-3b-logs.txt (snip of request/response traces and qlen stats).

Next steps:
- We're collecting full host-level traces and will produce a postmortem.
- Engineering will evaluate guardrails for kernel-selection heuristics and add a canary policy for runtime changes.

Diego/Marissa will coordinate a short call if you'd like a live walk-through.

Thanks for flagging this, Taylor.

- Marissa

Hi Taylor — following up with a recovery update and provisional timeline for the postmortem.

Recap:
- Incident window: ~14:47 UTC (deploy) to ~16:10 UTC (majority recovery).
- Primary measurable impact: transient 502/504 rate peaked at ~14% across your pinned pool; client-visible errors dropped below 1% by 16:10 UTC.

What we did:
1) Rolled back the kernel-selection heuristic on affected Artemis-3B hosts (15:58 UTC).
2) Temporarily tuned queue backpressure and KV pinning for accounts with sustained high throughput.
3) Implemented additional request logging for post-incident analysis.

Why it happened (short):
- A recent runtime change that attempts to select lower-latency kernels for longer contexts misrouted certain requests into a path that caused repetitive KV cache eviction and synchronous fallbacks, which in turn amplified queue latency until queues saturated and returned 502/504s.

Planned follow-ups:
- Full postmortem doc (link below) with root cause, timeline, user impact, and concrete action items for prevention. Target delivery: 2028-04-19 EOD.
- Immediate engineering actions: add feature-flagged canaries for kernel heuristics; add an automated rollback trigger if 5xx > 2% for >5 minutes on a host pool.
- Customer safety action: For customers pinned to Artemis-3B with strict SLOs, we will offer to pin to a verified stable runtime variant (Lumina-3B-verified) while we validate changes. If you'd like us to switch routing for Acme, reply and we can schedule a low-risk switchover.

If you prefer a quick call to review the postmortem draft, we have availability today 16:00–17:00 UTC.

Best,

Hi Taylor — attaching the incident postmortem and a short remediation plan. Thanks again for the rapid report and sample IDs.

Executive summary:
- Incident ID: INC-2987
- Impact window: 2028-04-17T14:47:00Z to 2028-04-17T16:10:00Z
- Root cause: kernel-selection heuristic incorrectly categorized long-context requests; induced KV cache eviction loop and queue saturation on a subset of Artemis-3B hosts.
- User impact: transient elevated 502/504 rates (peak ~14%) affecting requests routed to the affected pool. Recovery after rollback reduced errors to <1%.

Key corrective actions completed:
- Rollback of heuristic (done).
- Queue backpressure tuning and KV prefix pinning (done).
- Additional logs collected and attached.

Planned engineering work (ETA):
- Canary policy for kernel-selection changes (QA + infra): 3 weeks.
- Automated rollback trigger (ops): 2 weeks.
- Runbook update for runtime deploys with explicit SLO gating: 1 week.

Customer remediation options for Acme:
1) Short-term routing switch to Lumina-3B-verified (no code changes required) — we can schedule during a low-traffic window.
2) Longer-term: collaborate on a dedicated pinning policy for your production routing, with proactive testing on representative load shapes.

I've uploaded the full postmortem: postmortem-artemis3b.pdf (attached) and a read-only review copy at: https://redwood.company/pm/ARTEMIS-3B-PM-452.
